title: Knowledge check: VBScript Classes and Object-Oriented Patterns

questions.prompt: Which subtopic is explicitly listed under “VBScript Classes and Object-Oriented Patterns” in the attached Classic ASP curriculum?
questions.explanation: The PDF lists “Introduction to VBScript classes” under lesson 30, “VBScript Classes and Object-Oriented Patterns”. The distractors belong to other lesson topics.

questions.prompt: When applying “VBScript Classes and Object-Oriented Patterns” in a legacy Classic ASP application, which approach is strongest?
options: Enable detailed errors for all public visitors.
Change several settings at once and infer which one fixed the issue.
Make the runtime assumptions explicit and test normal, invalid, and boundary values.
Assume every value from a browser is trustworthy.
questions.answer_key: Make the runtime assumptions explicit and test normal, invalid, and boundary values.
questions.explanation: This approach keeps vbscript classes and object-oriented patterns testable and respects Classic ASP/IIS runtime boundaries. The exact IIS, provider, or component behavior must be checked in the target test environment.

questions.prompt: Before marking work on “VBScript Classes and Object-Oriented Patterns” ready for review, what evidence should be recorded?
options: Treat a successful happy-path test as proof of all security properties.
Document the observed result, tool/runtime version, and one meaningful failure or edge case.
Claim the production deployment passed without running it.
Delete diagnostic evidence before recording the outcome.
questions.answer_key: Document the observed result, tool/runtime version, and one meaningful failure or edge case.
questions.explanation: Good maintenance evidence includes the expected and observed result, relevant version/runtime assumptions, and a boundary or failure test. Never claim an execution/deployment test that was not run.
